_comment: Which scorer each lane invokes, and how.  Edited by hand when an engine's
CLI changes; read by bin/fidelity/engines.py.  A lane with pinned:false
refuses to plan -- see the module docstring for why guessing flags is worse
Verify a lane after editing:  bin/measure-local --probe-engines

sealed-ep8.name: k6_student_capture + k6_kld_report (sealed EP8 lane)

timing.provenance: ESTIMATE, NOT MEASURED. No per-window wall clock was recorded for the sealed EP8 lane in a form this runner can cite. The figure is a deliberately conservative placeholder so the cost estimate errs high rather than low; the max-runtime coherence check uses it, and the printed estimate labels it. Replace it with a measured number from a sealed-lane run receipt.

notes: This is the lane K6 and Q4 were measured with, and the only one whose
flags are verified against the file in this checkout.  EP size is
env-driven (QP_GLM53_EP_SIZE) and the launcher's --nproc-per-node must
match it.  Requires the patched quant_pipeline tree (--pipeline-root)
and a BF16 skeleton carrying config.json + model.safetensors.index.json,
because the capture binds inventory.config_sha256/index_sha256 to the
LOCAL files.
--surface packed dereferences packed_root from the checkpoint's own
materialization-receipt.json.  For a third-party artifact that path is
on the producer's machine; see hfmeta.sniff_surface, which detects this
before any money is spent.
sealed-ep8.surfaces_note: k6_student_capture.py --surface {packed,dione}, verified against the file. 'packed' additionally needs the payload store to be PUBLISHED in the repo; sniff_surface traps the case where the receipt's packed_root points at the producer's machine. There is no 'tr3-published' reader on THIS lane; the streaming lane gained one in M2 (stream_score --source tr3).

The full 2026-08-28 divergence findings are preserved in bin/README.md under 'History: the 2026-08 flag reconciliation' and in the JOURNAL entry.
streaming.launcher_note: launched under FIDELITY_PYTHON by the runner (the engine needs torch + transformers>=5.16 + quant_pipeline; preflight refuses with remedies when any is missing)
streaming.profile_map_note: 4.0-bpw now maps to tr3-4bpw: a SEALED TR3-published EXL3/MCG release (brandonmusic's layout and its byte-identical mirrors) read by stream_score --source tr3. 4.05/3.05 map to the stock-exllamav3 (exl3hf) profiles turbo-4.05bpw/turbo-3.05bpw. Dione 4-bpw snapshots are a DIFFERENT surface at the same nominal rate and remain sealed-lane only. stream_score --profile choices: k6,k8,k6k8,native-bf16,turbo-4.05bpw,turbo-3.05bpw,tr3-4bpw,mlx,gguf,nvfp4. k6k8 is reachable only by explicit --profile, never by bpw inference (6.68 is not a bpw key). || M3: profile_map_by_surface now resolves the profile from (surface, bits) before the bpw-only map is consulted. A 4.0-bpw Dione release and a 4.0-bpw TR3 release are the same number and different everything else; keying on bits alone would have labelled one as the other, and the old `or 'k6'` fallback would have labelled an unmapped rate as a K6 payload-store run.

scorer.device_policy: cpu-or-cuda; mps refused (fp64 accumulation cannot run on MPS -- torch TypeError)

timing.provenance: MEASURED on the K6 streaming panel run (stream-k6/runs/stream-run1, 1x H200 spot, --decode-cache none): capture-receipt elapsed_seconds 11,018.9 for 25 windows = 7.35 min/window; cold run 2 was 10,488.7 s = 6.99 min/window. Two cold runs of a 231 GB payload store therefore cost 5.97 GPU-hours (~$11.89 at $1.99/GPU-h), not the ~$7.50 the earlier estimate implied. The BF16-floor lane (--source native, 609 GB read per window) measured ~8.3 min/window on the same box class. || exl3hf surface (stock exllamav3, mul1) NOW MEASURED, 2026-08-29, turboderp/GLM-5.3-Flash-exl3 4.05bpw on 1x H200 spot: cold run 1 elapsed_seconds 4685.15 for 25 windows = 3.12 min/window, decoding 907,200 K4 expert matrices (42 layers x 288 experts x 3 projections x 25 windows). That is 2.4x FASTER than the K6 payload store's 7.35 min/window: the routed payloads are K4 rather than K6 and are read from the artifact's own HF shards rather than a content-addressed store. The planner still prices with 7.35 (the conservative direction) until a second exl3hf artifact confirms the figure. Materialize was estimated at 0.35 h and MEASURED at 2m06s. || tr3 surface (TR3-published exl3-mcg, K4, routed-experts-only): shares the exl3hf fill loop and payload shape, so the exl3hf measurement (3.12 min/window) is the closest evidence; the planner still prices with 7.35 (conservative). || SUPERSEDED 2026-08-30 (M2): the planner now prices with 2.82 min/window. Two independent artifacts on the artifact's-own-HF-shards path now agree and the K6 figure was never about this path: exl3hf (turboderp 4.05bpw, mul1) measured 3.12, and tr3 (brandonmusic's 4bpw via the Mia-AiLab mirror, mcg) measured 2.814 and 2.813 min/window on its two cold runs -- 4221.7 s and 4219.5 s for 25 windows each, 907,200 K4 expert matrices per run, peak 47.1 GB allocated on one H200. 7.35 was the K6 PAYLOAD-STORE figure: K6 payloads out of a content-addressed store, not K4 payloads out of the release's own shards. Keeping it made every plan for this family 2.6x too expensive, which is the wrong kind of conservative once two artifacts have measured the same path. || M3 (2026-08-30), dione surface (0xSero 3.0bpw, K3, TP4-sliced, 1x H200 spot): cold run 1 elapsed_seconds 4738.67 and run 2 4815.33 for 25 windows = 3.159 and 3.210 min/window, peak 47.07 GB allocated. That is SLOWER than tr3's 2.81 on the same lane and the same panel, and the reason is the storage layout rather than the rate: one Dione matrix is FOUR independently quantized TP-rank slices that are decoded separately and concatenated, so a K3 run does 4x the decode calls of a K4 tr3 run for the same 907,200 matrices. A single lane-wide constant cannot express that, so minutes_per_window_by_surface now carries the measured figure per surface and the lane-wide value stays as the fallback for a surface with no measurement yet.

notes: Known properties from the validation run, which the receipt must disclose: bitwise
cross-topology parity is impossible (routed-expert combine order moves logits rms
0.26-0.28); streaming runs ARE bitwise identical to each other, so determinism holds
WITHIN the lane; peak 34-47 GB on one H200 as currently scheduled.
Inputs are THIS CAMPAIGN'S encode output (packed root with contract.json +
inventory.json + mtp-adapter-receipt.json + payload-store/{objects,choices}) plus a
--bf16 tree -- with the ONE exception of --source native (--inventory + --bf16 only).
at plan time, for $0.00 (see surfaces below).
NEW 2026-08-29: --capture-role teacher turns a native run into a SAME-LANE teacher
(k6/SAME-LANE-TEACHER.md); --store-positions per-window:<m> produces a PREVIEW
capture no sealed consumer accepts.

NEW 2026-08-29 (M2): 'tr3-published' IS now readable (--source tr3). It is the only third-party surface here whose publisher seals it: tr3_surface.verify_seal recomputes all 12 claims of exl3-mcg-storage-abi.json + materialization-receipt.json from the published bytes BEFORE decoding, so its rows carry a seal verification instead of an unsealed_source caveat.
streaming.surfaces_note: stream_score.py --source {checkpoint,payload-store,dione,native,exl3hf,tr3}. 'packed' needs the payload store published; 'native-bf16' needs only --inventory + --bf16; 'exl3hf' reads a stock-exllamav3 HF-sharded release (mul1/mcg codebook, full-scope quant incl. quantized lm_head) and needs --bf16 pointing at the tree exl3hf_surface.py materialize produced from the SAME snapshot; 'tr3-published' reads a SEALED TR3 release (exl3-mcg, routed experts ONLY, native BF16 head) via tr3_surface; 'dione' reads an UNSEALED 0xSero selective-EXL3 release (exl3-mcg, routed experts of layers 3-44 only, TP4-sliced storage, everything else retained at source precision incl. the head) via dione_surface. tr3-published and dione both need --bf16 pointing at the non-routed tree their own materializer wrote from the SAME snapshot: their non-routed tensors ARE the official ones, but they cannot serve transformers out of the artifact's shards (tr3 interleaves them with routed payloads; dione's retained shards also carry the 864 MTP expert tensors) and transformers keys its checkpoint load off the shard FILES.

timing.provenance: decode 16-20 ms/matrix at 6/4 bpw MPS MEASURED (bin/selftest_decode_parity.py on a 128 GB M4 Max) -> 9.7-12.1 min per full 36,288-matrix decode pass; the KDA/DSA/mHC trunk forward on MPS is UNMEASURED (34 of 45 layers are Kimi-Delta linear attention whose fast paths are Triton/CUDA) -- run `bin/measure-local --fixture fetch` for the fixture-scale datum, then one real window. No number is invented here: minutes_per_window stays null until one is measured.

notes: --unpack-device cpu is a FIXED flag: the MPS int64 unpack escape, decode still
bitwise identical to CPU (selftest_decode_parity).  fp64 KLD accumulation cannot
run on MPS at all; the scorer (bin/kld_preview.py) pins it to CPU and says so.
Receipts from this lane are PREVIEWS: the lane differs from the teacher's and its
floor against the sealed teacher is unmeasured; kld_preview labels them
structurally unsubmittable.
Perf levers that are real today: --decode-cache disk (Apple internal NVMe ~5-6 GB/s
vs the floor box's 0.9; needs 609 GB free -- measure before assuming), --chunk-positions
512 for the scorer.  --window-batch/--expert-chunk are NOT engine flags.

bf16-floor.name: stream_score --source native (the lane's BF16 measurement floor)

timing.provenance: MEASURED on 1x H200 spot (IN2, 28 vCPU, 300 GiB cgroup) reading the 599 GB BF16 tree off a CephFS filesystem at ~1.05 GB/s with 28 reader threads: window 1 (cold, all 42 layers filled) 678 s; steady-state windows 483-549 s with --decode-cache ram holding 17 of 42 layers. See k6/BF16-FLOOR.md.

notes: This lane does not score a quant. It scores the UN-QUANTIZED BF16 experts through the
identical capture, so its panel mean is the FLOOR every quant measured on this lane
sits on top of. Subtract it (k6/tools/bf16_floor_summary.py) to state a quant's
quantization-attributable error.
It is the only stream_score source that needs NO packed root: --inventory (a sealed
quant-pipeline.glm-release-inventory.v1) plus the --bf16 tree is the whole input.
It is IO-bound, not decode-bound: 14.50 GB of routed BF16 per layer, 42 layers per
window. Size the box by filesystem read bandwidth and by 47.1 GB of VRAM, not by
matmul throughput.
Requires SM90-class or newer ONLY in the sense that the venv is pinned to torch
2.11.0+cu130; an instance whose driver predates CUDA 13 cannot run it at all
(observed on an A100-80GB image shipping driver 12080).
The workspace symlink farm (/workspace/artifacts/...) must exist before the run: the
sealed panel receipt declares those paths and the artifact identity check refuses
symlinked FILES while requiring the directories to resolve.
bf16-floor.surfaces_note: The official BF16 release tree itself (config.json + model.safetensors.index.json + shards). Not a reader for a third-party quant.
